14-030.r: Equal pay for equal work → deduced by the Supreme Court from 'Socialist' in the Preamble read with Articles 14, 16 and 39(d).
hi: Equal pay for equal work (समान कार्य के लिए समान वेतन)

14-031.r: Randhir Singh v. Union of India → 'Equal pay for equal work' deduced from Articles 14 and 16 read with the Preamble ('Socialist') and Article 39(d).

14-032.r: Article 17 → untouchability abolished; its practice in any form forbidden; enforcing any disability arising from it is an offence punishable by law.

14-037.r: Article 17 (abolition of untouchability) is a 'statement of principle' to end humiliation of Dalits and secure their fundamental, socio-economic, political and cultural rights.

14-038.r: Protection against untouchability (Article 17) is part of the Right to Equality, not the Right against Exploitation or Right to Freedom.

14-039.r: Untouchability is ended by laws, better education and public awareness, not by providing jobs; Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955 made it a punishable offence.
hi: Protection of Civil Rights Act (नागरिक अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम)

14-040.r: Both true, R explains A: untouchability is a worst form of structural violence (built into social structure), practised in the name of religious sanctions.

14-041.r: Articles 14, 15, 16 → Right to Equality; Article 19 → Right to Freedom (speech, peaceful assembly, associations). By this grouping Article 19 is the odd one.
14-041.c: Book marks none because two groupings work: Article 19 is a Right to Freedom while 14, 15 and 16 are Right to Equality; and Article 14 alone covers foreigners too (15, 16 and 19 are for citizens only).

14-042.r: Right to Freedom → Articles 19 to 22: 19 freedoms (speech, assembly, association, movement, residence); 20 protection in conviction for offences; 21 life and personal liberty.

14-043.r: Article 19(1) guarantees 6 freedoms (speech, assembly, associations, movement, residence, profession); freedom to own, acquire and dispose of property is not among them.

14-044.r: Article 19(1): speech and expression (a), assemble peaceably (b), practise any profession (g). Equal opportunity in public employment is Article 16 (Right to Equality), not Right to Freedom.

14-046.r: Freedom of the Press → not expressly in the Constitution; the Supreme Court held it is part of freedom of speech and expression, Article 19(1)(a).
hi: Freedom of the Press (प्रेस की स्वतंत्रता)

14-048.r: Press freedom is not explicit in the Constitution; it is included in Article 19(1)(a), freedom of speech and expression.

14-049.r: Freedom of newspapers → within Article 19(1)(a); Sakal Papers Ltd v. Union of India (1961): press freedom is part of freedom of speech and expression.

14-050.r: Supreme Court: hoisting the National Flag atop private buildings is every citizen's fundamental right under Article 19(1)(a).

14-051.r: Article 19(1)(b) → assemble peaceably and without arms; Article 19(3) → reasonable restrictions for public order. Gheraoing officials is not covered.

14-052.r: Article 19(2) grounds: sovereignty and integrity, security of State, foreign relations, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to offence; not 'unbecoming criticism'.

14-053.r: Article 19(2) restrictions on speech include security of State, defamation and public order; 'sedition' is not a listed ground.
14-053.t: Sedition is not an Article 19(2) ground; 'incitement to an offence' is.

14-054.r: Reasonable restrictions (Articles 19(2) to 19(6)) must safeguard general public interest and may reflect prevailing social values and needs; Directive Principles cannot be bypassed.

14-055.r: Article 21 → protection of life and personal liberty. Article 19 → freedoms of speech etc.; 20 → conviction for offences; 22 → arrest and detention.

14-056.r: Article 21: no person deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law; the question links due process to Article 21.

14-057.r: Right to travel abroad → Article 21; Maneka Gandhi v. UOI (1978).

14-058.r: Maneka Gandhi 1978 (7 judges): Articles 14, 19, 21 not mutually exclusive; life includes dignity; procedure close to US procedural due process. Petitioner-burden statement is wrong.

14-059.r: SC-recognised Fundamental Rights: Right to Shelter (Chameli Singh v. State of U.P. 1995, Article 21), Right to Travel Abroad (Satwant Singh), Equal Pay for Equal Work.

14-060.r: Right to privacy → implicit in Article 21 (with 19(1)(d)); Govind v. State of M.P. (1975), Malak Singh v. State of Punjab (1980); 'right to be let alone'.

14-061.r: Right to Privacy → intrinsic part of Article 21 and the freedoms in Part III (Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India).

14-062.r: K.S. Puttaswamy case (nine-judge bench, 24 August 2017): Right to Privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21, part of the Part III freedoms.

14-064.r: Right to marry a person of one's choice → Article 21 (Lata Singh v. State of U.P., 2006; Hadiya case: right to choose a partner).

14-065.r: Article 21 covers medical aid to the injured, safety from sexual harassment at work, pollution-free water; capital punishment is not barred by it (Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab).

14-066.r: After 44th Amendment (1978), Article 21 (life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended even in National Emergency; Article 19 rights auto-suspended if Emergency is on war or external aggression.
14-066.h: 44 fixed 21: after the 44th Amendment, Article 21 never goes.

14-067.r: Unnikrishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993) → Right to Education flows from Article 21; free education for children up to 14 years.

14-068.r: Right to Education (6-14 years) is a Fundamental Right: Eighty-Sixth Amendment Act 2002 inserted Article 21A; RTE Act 2009; added from 1 April 2010.

14-071.r: Article 21A: State gives free and compulsory education to children aged six to fourteen; education is indispensable to the right to development as a human right (R explains A).

14-072.r: Right against Exploitation → Article 23 (no human trafficking, begar, forced labour) and Article 24 (no child below fourteen in factory, mine, hazardous work). Untouchability (Article 17) is not.
hi: Right against Exploitation (शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार)

14-073.r: Article 24 → no child under 14 years employed in any factory, mine or other hazardous employment.

14-074.r: Article 24's ban on employing children below fourteen in factories, mines or hazardous work is an absolute prohibition.

14-075.r: Article 20: no ex-post facto law, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination. Protection from torture comes under Article 21, not 20. Child exploitation → Article 24.
14-075.h: Article 20 = three 'No's: ex-post facto, double jeopardy, self-incrimination.

14-078.r: Child rights → Article 24 of the ICCPR; Article 24 of the Indian Constitution also protects children.
14-078.h: Same number twice: 24 in ICCPR and 24 in our Constitution.

14-079.r: Article 20(2) → no one punished twice for the same offence (double jeopardy); Article 20(3) → no self-incrimination.

14-080.r: Article 20(3) → an accused cannot be compelled to be a witness against himself (self-incrimination); accused presumed innocent till guilt is proved.

14-081.r: Article 20(2) → no one prosecuted and punished twice for the same offence: Doctrine of Double Jeopardy (maxim: Nemo Debet Bis Vexari).

14-082.r: Article 22 → an arrested person must be told the grounds of arrest and may consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice.

14-083.r: Wrong pair: Article 22(2) is not about Parliament allowing detention beyond three months; 22(2) → arrested person produced before nearest magistrate within twenty-four hours.

14-084.r: Article 22(4) → a preventive detention law cannot authorise detention for longer than 3 months.

14-085.r: Preventive detention: a person can be detained without trial for at most three months (Article 22(4)).

14-086.r: Article 355 → Union must protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance (true). POTA 2002 made confession before police admissible; Article 22(5) lets detainee make representation.
14-086.c: Book prints (a), but statement 2 is also correct: Article 22(3) denies preventive detainees the right to consult a lawyer. With statement 1 true and 3 false, the answer is (b) Only two.

14-087.r: Parole is not a right in India (claim not absolute, even with a sufficient case); State Governments have their own Prisoners Release on Parole Rules.

14-088.r: Article 25 → freedom of conscience, profession, practice, propagation of religion; Sikhs may wear and carry Kirpans; State can legislate social reform. No right of religious bodies to convert people.

14-091.r: 'Hindu' in Article 25 includes Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists; it does not include Parsis.

14-092.r: Article 25 freedom of religion is subject to public order, morality and health; 'humanism' is not a limit.
14-092.h: Religion's limits = 'PMH': Public order, Morality, Health.

14-093.r: Article 26 (religious denominations manage own affairs, institutions, property) → subject to public order, morality and health only.
14-093.t: National security, education and secularism are not Article 26 limits.

14-094.r: Wrong pair: Article 29 → protection of minorities' interests; minorities' right to establish and administer educational institutions → Article 30. Articles 23, 24, 26 pairs are correct.
